subject: Competitive swap: pricing anchors, packaging questions, and contract caveats
messages:
From: Dan O'Neil <dan@swapcloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial numbers and migration assumptions (SwapCloud -> Redwood)

Jonas —

Thanks again for taking the intro call yesterday. Per our conversation I promised a quick sketch of the commercial picture if SwapCloud were to move to Redwood. Attached is a compact TCO spreadsheet that shows a 12-month run-rate comparison (VM hours + egress + feature add-ons).

Top-line: SwapCloud's procurement team is looking for parity on list price + a one-time onboarding credit to offset rollout costs. They referenced a competing offer that includes three months of credits plus a reduced per-token list rate for the first 6 months.

Questions for you:
- Do you have flexibility on a short-term list-rate concession (6 months) for a committed 12-month term?
- Can we offer any onboarding credits tied to milestone completion (pilot success -> go-live)?
- Any contractual caveats (audit, egress caps, termination fees) that will materially differ and should be surfaced early?

I attached the spreadsheet (swapcloud_tco_summary.xlsx). If you want a short call tomorrow to align on a proposal I can loop in procurement.

—Dan
Account Exec, SwapCloud

Attachments: swapcloud_tco_summary.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: Dan O'Neil <dan@swapcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial numbers and migration assumptions (SwapCloud -> Redwood)

Dan —

Thanks for the spreadsheet. Quick replies inline:

- Short-term list-rate concession: possible, yes. We usually structure this as a step-down rebate (applied as a credit) for months 1–6 tied to a minimum committed spend. We prefer credits to changing the published rate to avoid downstream billing surprises for the account team.
- Onboarding credit: yes, we can do a milestone-based onboarding credit (pilot completion + production ingest). We typically cap onboarding credits at ~10–15% of first-year committed spend for customers of this size.
- Contract caveats: key things to highlight early — egress policy (we have tiered egress pricing), data retention & CCPA/SOC2 attestation language, and a standard termination clause with a 30-day notice; exceptions for force-majeure or regulatory orders.

I'll loop Laura from Commercial Ops and Karthik from Pricing to scope the feasible credit buckets and any SLA carveouts. Can you share the competing offer (redacted pricing line items are fine)? That helps us calibrate the anchor.

If you're open to it, let's do a 30-min alignment tomorrow at 10am PT.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial numbers and migration assumptions (SwapCloud -> Redwood)

Team —

Forwarding SwapCloud's request. They want price parity + onboarding credits; they've been presented a vendor swap package that includes 3 months free + a 6-month discount off list.

Notes / proposed approach:
1) Commercial structure: propose a spend-committed 12-month term with a 6-month rebate applied as monthly credits (not a permanent list-rate change). This preserves public list integrity and aligns incentives.
2) Onboarding credit: offer up to 12% of first-year committed spend, paid out for reach of two milestones (pilot completion, end of month 2 post-ingest).
3) Escrow / termination caveat: include an accelerated egress assistance clause (discounted egress for 60 days) if SwapCloud needs a rollback window.
4) Approval ask: need an exception for the onboarding credit % (Karthik) and confirmation that we can commit to the 60-day egress assistance (Laura).

Attachments: redwood_terms_vs_swapcloud_redlines.pdf (I will attach later in the thread after legal redlines)

Can we keep this tight — goal is to have a clean commercial letter by EOD Thursday so Dan can present to procurement next week.

—Jonas

From: Maria Ruiz <maria@swapcloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: Dan O'Neil <dan@swapcloud.com>, procurement@swapcloud.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive swap: pricing anchors, packaging questions, and contract caveats

Jonas / Laura / Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement asked us to clarify two items before they will consider presenting Redwood as a replacement: 1) the exact mechanics of the 6-month rebate (is it applied as invoice credits or an end-of-term true-up?), and 2) the onboarding credit payout schedule and any clawback provisions if we terminate early.

Procurement also requested that any egress assistance be explicitly timeboxed (they prefer 60 days) and that the onboarding credit be tied to measurable acceptance criteria (we can provide a short runbook for pilot acceptance).

Dan will send the competing offer redacted tonight — procurement needs to see the numeric delta. If you can produce a clean one-page commercial with the rebate mechanics and the milestone list/cap schedule, that will speed things.

Thanks,
Maria Ruiz
Director, Cloud Procurement | SwapCloud

Attachments referenced: swapcloud_tco_summary.xlsx
